TK Kirkland returns to VladTV to react to the latest developments in the Yella Beezy trial connected to the 2020 killing of Dallas rapper Mo3. Vlad breaks down the history of the Dallas rap beef, the freeway shooting that led to Mo3’s death, and the convicted gunman’s claim that Yella Beezy allegedly paid for the hit — an allegation now being tested in court.

Kirkland gives his blunt “old school” perspective on the widely shared highway footage, questioning why Mo3 left his vehicle and why bystanders didn’t intervene as the armed suspect ran through traffic. Watch the full discussion for context on hip-hop conflict, street decisions, and the legal questions still unfolding.

recentItems.title: Ossi Ketola on Losing Millions From Valve’s Crackdown and the Crypto Crash (Part 4)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 3: https://youtu.be/SSpqSAia4fc
Part 1: https://youtu.be/xq9iv5h0X0o
--------
Ossi Ketola sits down with Vlad to explain how Valve’s crackdown on Counter-Strike skin gambling reshaped the entire marketplace—and nearly wiped him out. Ketola breaks down how U.S. legal pressure pushed Valve to ban trading bots used by gambling sites, forcing competitors to shut down or pivot into crypto gambling. He details how Empire survived by building a difficult peer-to-peer trading system that connected users directly, creating what he describes as a near-monopoly in the space.

Ketola also opens up about the financial pressure behind the scenes: a crypto-heavy portfolio that fell from nearly $20 million to about $2 million during the Bitcoin crash, while his businesses were burning roughly $600,000 a month. From “suicide bots” to liquidity problems and the risks of holding wealth in crypto, this conversation offers a rare look inside Counter-Strike skins, online gambling, and high-stakes entrepreneurship.

Anthony Scaramucci sits down with Vlad for a candid conversation about marriage, money, divorce, and reconciliation after his turbulent 2017 White House stint. The SkyBridge founder clarifies the timeline of his first divorce in 2014, discusses why he gave his ex-wife significant liquid assets despite New York’s 50/50 divorce laws, and explains how his public financial disclosure became part of the conversation. Scaramucci also opens up about signing a prenup before his second marriage—then later legally tearing it up as a “burn the boats” commitment while rebuilding trust with his wife after she filed for divorce during the political fallout. The discussion touches on family, wealth, and the emotional cost of public life, with Scaramucci comparing reconciliation to a broken bone healing stronger. He also shares how friend Ben Stiller and his wife reconnected during COVID, offering another perspective on relationships that nearly ended but survived.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/AxHbPY_r1q4
--------
Carlos Lehder sits down with Vlad to revisit George “Boston George” Jung’s final cocaine case, his 60-year prison sentence, and their fractured partnership after Jung testified against him. Lehder discusses the 2001 film *Blow*, starring Johnny Depp as Jung and Diego Delgado as Lehder, saying he enjoyed the movie but believes key parts were fictionalized. Most notably, Lehder claims Jung never met Pablo Escobar, arguing the Medellín Cartel boss would not risk meeting an American he viewed as a “walking indictment.”

Lehder points to testimony from *United States v. Carlos Lehder* in Jacksonville, Florida, including a disputed story about driving from Medellín to Escobar’s Hacienda Nápoles. He also references his attorney Edward Shohat and his later cooperation with the U.S. government. A revealing look at drug history, Hollywood mythmaking, and the real stories behind *Blow*, George Jung, and Pablo Escobar.

--------
In this candid interview, Harlem rapper G.Dep reflects on the moment he returned to a police precinct to confess details from a years-old shooting, only to learn investigators had matched his account to a homicide. The former Bad Boy Records artist explains how the revelation affected him as he was preparing music around *Ghetto Legend*, following the legacy of *Child of the Ghetto*. He also discusses why his lawyer pushed for a trial despite his confession, the guilty verdict, and the 15-years-to-life sentence that followed.

G.Dep responds to the victim’s stepbrother calling him an “idiot” for reopening painful family wounds, explaining that he understood the anger and could not control how the family processed the confession. A sobering conversation about accountability, trauma, hip-hop, the criminal justice system, and the consequences of choices made decades earlier.
